messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f
messages.subject: Incompatibility with package circular
parts:
Hi again

(it seems it's bug uncovering day for me today ;) )

ggplot choques on objects produced by the package "circular", which is
meant to deal with angles. circular introduces as new "circular" class
which gives useful information such as rotation direction, unit,
origin etc. Objects of class circular are also of class numeric so
ggplot should be able to deal with that part.

library("ggplot2")
install.packages("circular")
library("circular")

t=data.frame(theta=runif(10), y=runif(10))
qplot(theta, y, data=t)
t=data.frame(y=runif(10), theta=runif(10))
# works ok

t$theta=circular(t$theta)

class(t$theta)
[1] "circular" "numeric"

qplot(theta, y, data=t)
Error in if (test == TRUE) { : argument is of length zero

ggplot(t)+geom_point(aes(x=theta, y=y))
Error in if (test == TRUE) { : argument is of length zero

ggplot(t)+geom_path(aes(x=theta, y=y))
Error in if (test == TRUE) { : argument is of length zero

ggplot(t)+geom_bar(aes(x=theta))
Error in if (test == TRUE) { : argument is of length zero


On this one I am stumped. I can't even find a "if (test == TRUE)" bit
in ggplot's code...

PS: for now:

t$theta = as.numeric(t$theta)
class(t$theta)
[1] "numeric"
ggplot(t)+geom_bar(aes(x=theta))

solves the problem.

JiHO
